R0014.title: Inventory Denial
R0014.definition: Exhausting the inventory of goods or services without completing a purchase or transaction.
R0014.description: By placing large numbers of orders without paying, driving all products in a merchant's store to zero inventory so the merchant has nothing to sell. Additionally, bulk adding items to cart or placing unpaid orders can be used to probe a merchant's inventory levels or actual purchase prices. While not necessarily aimed at exhausting inventory, the harm caused is the same or greater.
R0014.influence: Common in commercial competition. Once inventory is exhausted, other users can no longer purchase the goods.

references.title: OWASP Automated Threat: OAT021 Denial of Inventory

observables: A single account or device fingerprint places bulk orders across many products within a short window with an extremely low payment rate
Product inventory is wiped out instantly and the corresponding orders concentrate and time out unpaid within minutes
A large volume of orders are added to cart then cancelled, with cart-operation frequency far exceeding normal user behavior
The same IP range or device cluster launches inventory-locking requests against all SKUs of a single merchant
Actual payment rate is severely inverted against inventory occupation, with a spike in refund/cancellation rates after ordering
